Kagiso Rabada is the Player of the Match

Kagiso Rabada (1/2): [How does it feel to have performed within all-round performance like this?] Yeah, we were a bit behind the eight ball on day one. Yeah, under pressure so we needed to fight back. So I'm glad that we could do that. And playing at the Wanderers again after some time. It's always special, a special ground for me, special ground for us. I guess we just would have liked to see more fans. [It was important for you to break the game open on that first morning?] Yeah, we knew how important it was because I guess we would have liked to bat first as well, knowing the nature of the pitch here on day one. It could be a bit slow and it was a bit slow, perhaps favouring the batters a bit more and wickets tends to quicken up as the game goes on. So credit to Bangladesh. I thought they applied themselves really well. But even more chuffed that we could fight back.

Rabada (2/2): [What is it that you actually work on in the nets with your batting?] To be honest, I haven't been working on it much. I think I spent about 20 minutes that entire week on my batting. Yeah, but in the middle is where you have to find a way to actually score some runs. And I'm glad that I could do it when we needed it most. [On the team motivation] Yes, I think it motivates us looking at the journey that we've been on in the past two years and looking to continue on that trajectory. I think we've proven it once again. Yeah, so it's really nice to see and hopefully we can do it for a lot longer.
